home.title: AML operations under control, from onboarding to audit.
home.lead: Duevio gives regulated firms one workspace to manage KYC, client files, ownership, reviews, tasks and evidence across the customer lifecycle.
home.overviewTitle: What a controlled AML environment looks like
home.highlight1: One client file instead of fragmented folders and emails
home.highlight2: A defined workflow from onboarding to review and evidence
home.highlight3: Essential, Professional and Enterprise paths in one platform
home.visualLead: A single visual thread from onboarding to every review, approval and audit-ready decision.
home.challengeTitle: AML becomes hard to defend when the evidence is scattered.
home.challengeLead: KYC data, ownership records, screening results, approvals, review dates and supporting documents lose context when they live in separate tools. Duevio keeps the operational record connected.
home.problem1: KYC data split between emails, folders and spreadsheets
home.problem2: Periodic reviews and document expiries managed manually
home.problem3: Ownership and UBO structures that are difficult to reconstruct
home.problem4: Screening results detached from the decisions they support
home.problem5: Approvals and exceptions without a complete audit trail
home.problem6: Audit requests that force teams to rebuild the file
home.whyTitle: One operating layer for the work behind AML compliance.
home.whyLead: Duevio is built for teams that already know their AML obligations and need a controlled, repeatable way to execute and evidence the work.
home.feature1Text: Keep onboarding data, documents, notes, checks and decisions in one organised client record.
home.feature2Text: Turn recurring AML activities into visible tasks, approvals, deadlines and review steps.
home.feature3Text: Make direct and indirect ownership, beneficial owners and key roles easy to review and maintain.
home.feature4Text: Preserve the chronology behind reviews, decisions and remediation so proof is available when requested.
home.compareTitle: Duevio connects onboarding, workflow, review and evidence.
home.compareLead: A standalone KYC tool can collect information. Duevio is designed to help teams run the work that continues after collection.
home.industriesTitle: Different sectors. Different controls. One AML operating model.
home.industriesLead: Duevio supports regulated businesses and professional firms with adaptable workflows and a consistent evidence structure.
home.trust1Text: Give compliance teams and management a clearer view of open actions, reviews and evidence.
home.trust2Text: Apply internal permissions to reviews, approvals and sensitive client information.
home.trust3Text: Keep actions and decisions connected to the client file and the people responsible for them.
home.trust4Text: Start online with Essential, then move to a guided or tailored setup as your organisation grows.

privacy.title: Privacy Notice
privacy.requiredText: Insert the verified legal name, registered address and privacy contact of the entity operating Duevio. GDPR Article 13 requires the controller's identity and contact details when personal data are collected.
privacy.p1: Duevio is the product name used for this service. The legal entity acting as controller for website enquiries, account creation and commercial communications must be identified in the production version of this notice.
privacy.p2: Depending on how you use the site, we may collect contact and organisation details, account registration information, support or demo requests, technical security logs, language and privacy preferences, and billing references. Payment card or PayPal credentials should be collected directly by the selected payment provider and not by this marketing website.
privacy.p3: We process data to answer enquiries and demo requests, create and administer accounts, provide contracted services, protect the service, meet legal obligations and, where you opt in, send marketing communications. The applicable legal basis may be performance of a contract or steps requested before a contract, compliance with legal obligations, legitimate interests in operating and securing the service, or consent where required.
privacy.p4: Data may be handled by authorised Duevio personnel and service providers needed for hosting, security, communications, customer support, billing and payment processing. A production privacy notice should identify relevant categories and, where appropriate, maintain a current subprocessor list.
privacy.p5: Where personal data is transferred outside the EEA, the production service must use an applicable transfer mechanism and provide information about the safeguards used, such as an adequacy decision or appropriate contractual safeguards.
privacy.p6: Personal data should be retained only for as long as necessary for the relevant purpose, contractual relationship, security need and applicable legal or regulatory retention period. Production retention periods or criteria must be documented for each main data category.
privacy.p7: Subject to the GDPR and applicable law, you may have rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability, and the right to withdraw consent where processing relies on consent. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a competent supervisory authority.
privacy.p8: Where Duevio processes personal data using automated or AI-assisted functions, the applicable controller must assess the GDPR requirements for profiling and automated decision-making, including Article 22 where relevant, and provide any additional information required by law.
privacy.p9: Duevio should apply technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, including access control, logging, secure transport, vulnerability management and data minimisation. Specific production controls should be documented separately from this public notice.
privacy.p10: The verified controller and privacy contact details must be inserted here before the site is released as the production legal notice.
cookies.title: Cookie and storage policy
cookies.p1: This prototype stores language and privacy preferences locally in your browser. These settings are used to provide the site and remember choices you make.
cookies.p2: No optional analytics service is enabled in this repository version. If analytics is added later and requires consent, it must remain disabled until you accept the relevant category.
cookies.p3: No marketing or advertising tracker is enabled in this repository version. Any future non-essential marketing technology must be documented and, where required, activated only after consent.
cookies.p5: Before production release, verify the actual cookies, local-storage keys and third-party technologies used by hosting, payment, support, analytics and embedded services, then update this policy with their purpose and duration.
ai.title: AI transparency and responsible use
ai.p1: This notice describes the transparency principles Duevio should apply where an AI-assisted function is enabled. It does not state that every Duevio module uses AI and it does not classify any unverified function as high-risk.
ai.h2: 2. Transparency at the point of use
ai.p2: Where an AI system is intended to interact directly with a natural person and the interaction is not obvious, the interface should clearly inform that person that they are interacting with an AI system, in line with Article 50 of the EU AI Act.
ai.p3: Where Duevio provides functions that generate or manipulate synthetic content, the provider and deployer responsibilities for machine-readable marking and user-facing disclosure should be assessed and implemented where Article 50 requires them.
ai.p4: AI-assisted outputs should be presented as support for qualified users. Compliance conclusions, customer risk decisions and regulatory actions require the organisation using Duevio to apply its own governance, policies and professional judgement.
ai.p5: Where Duevio personnel or customer personnel operate AI systems, the relevant provider or deployer should implement AI-literacy measures appropriate to the users' knowledge, experience and the context of use, as required by Article 4 of the EU AI Act.
ai.p6: AI functionality that processes personal data remains subject to the GDPR. Controllers should assess lawful basis, transparency, data minimisation, security, retention, profiling and automated decision-making requirements before deployment.
ai.p7: Before any AI-assisted module is placed in production, its actual purpose, inputs, outputs, users and decision impact should be documented so the applicable role, risk classification and obligations under the AI Act can be determined from the real implementation.
terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.requiredText: The contracting legal entity, registered details, governing law, jurisdiction, support commitments, refund rules and final liability provisions must be completed and legally reviewed before these terms can be used for live contracting.
terms.p1: Duevio provides software tools for AML operations, client onboarding, file management, reviews, workflow and evidence management. The exact features available depend on the selected plan and implementation.
terms.p2: Duevio is a software service. The customer remains responsible for its legal, regulatory and compliance obligations, policies, risk appetite, decisions and filings.
terms.p3: Customers must provide accurate account information, keep credentials secure, configure the service appropriately, authorise only permitted users and use the service lawfully.
terms.p4: Essential is offered online at the displayed price unless a different commercial offer applies. Professional and Enterprise pricing and implementation terms are agreed separately. Taxes, renewal terms, cancellation rights and refund rules must be confirmed in the production commercial terms.
terms.p5: Customer data remains subject to the applicable contract, data-processing terms and confidentiality obligations. A production SaaS agreement should define controller and processor roles, security commitments, subprocessing and return or deletion of data.
terms.p6: Duevio and its software, branding and documentation remain protected by applicable intellectual-property rights. Customers receive only the rights needed to use the service under the agreed subscription.
terms.p7: Production service levels, support channels, maintenance windows and incident handling must be specified in the applicable plan or contract.
terms.p8: The final contract should define when access may be suspended or terminated, including non-payment, security risk, misuse or legal requirements, together with data-export and deletion arrangements.
terms.p9: The production agreement must include legally reviewed warranty, exclusion and liability provisions appropriate to the contracting entity, customer type and applicable law.
terms.p10: Insert the verified contracting entity, governing law, jurisdiction and formal contact details before production use.
